audit_findings.title: A potentially material Hewitt environmental claim is neither accrued nor bridged
audit_findings.magnitude: $370.5m publicly reported LADWP cost pool ($92.0m NHW, $245.0m NHC, $11.5m study and $22.0m wells), before operating costs; Vulcan's share unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An unrecorded obligation would be deducted in the equity bridge; continuing treatment-system costs could also reduce normalized OE.
audit_findings.evidence: However, as discussions continue with LADWP and as additional records and data are analyzed, it is reasonably possible that an estimated material loss could be recognized in the near term.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved liability, not a demonstrated valuation adjustment. Nevertheless, the latest filing still says a material loss is reasonably possible, and the identified LADWP cost pool equals 2.4% of the $15,477m base equity value before additional operating costs. That scale is reasonably capable of affecting intrinsic value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the January 2026 demand, subsequent correspondence, technical allocation studies and insurance information; estimate Vulcan's share of LADWP, EPA and Honeywell costs and rerun the bridge and OE if any recurring costs are not already captured.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter may value California concrete earnings after the business was sold or committed for sale
audit_findings.magnitude: $722.1m combined California and U.S. Virgin Islands proceeds ($572.1m cash plus a $150.0m note with $139.7m recorded present value); California-specific proceeds and sustainable OE unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The 2025 anchor includes earnings from operations sold in June 2026, while the bridge must separately recognize only the remaining sale proceeds or assets not already reflected in cash, debt, shares or other balances.
audit_findings.evidence: During the fourth quarter of 2025, we entered into an agreement to sell our ready-mixed concrete business in California.
audit_findings.explanation: A perimeter mismatch is demonstrated because the California sale closed before the valuation date while the perimeter is null. Retaining disposed earnings overstates operating value, but omitting the sale note or other remaining proceeds understates bridge value. The $722.1m combined proceeds equal 4.7% of base equity value, so the net effect could be material even though the California portion is not separately filed.
audit_findings.action: Separate California from U.S. Virgin Islands proceeds and earnings, remove California's sustainable OE from the anchor, and reconcile the cash proceeds, $150.0m note, restricted cash, acquisitions, repurchases and other uses through the valuation date before rerunning all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Asset-retirement cash obligations may disappear through the DDA&A add-back
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed ARO liability was $464.5m at June 30, 2026, 2025 ARO operating costs were $35.1m, and 2025 settlements were $17.6m including $1.0m noncash
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back ARO accretion and retirement-cost depreciation without deducting cash settlements or a normalized reclamation reserve increases OE.
audit_findings.evidence: As described in Note 17 , our asset retirement obligations totaled $ 456.5 million as of December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate substantial ARO charges, settlements and liabilities, but the supplied record does not show whether the OE worksheet already captures cash settlements through operating cash flow or a separate adjustment. Therefore an error is possible but neither its existence nor its normalized annual magnitude is established.
audit_findings.action: Trace every year's OE from net income or operating cash flow through the DDA&A add-back; identify ARO accretion, deferred-cost depreciation, cash settlements and settlement gains or losses, then rerun with a normalized reclamation deduction if those cash obligations are missing.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 anchor may retain a disposed business and its sale gain
audit_findings.magnitude: $42.4m pretax Houston disposal gain, equal to 3.9% of the $1,087.7m anchor OE; Houston's recurring pre-sale OE unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A disposal gain or earnings from operations no longer owned would inflate anchor OE and every projected year; any surviving proceeds belong in the bridge only once.
audit_findings.evidence: The 2025 gain on sale of property, plant & equipment and businesses of $52.4 million includes a pretax gain of $42.4 million from the sale of our asphalt mix and construction paving operations in Houston, Texas.
audit_findings.explanation: The Houston disposition and gain are demonstrated, but their treatment in the OE worksheet is not. The filed gain provides a measurable potential distortion, while the recurring contribution of the sold operations is unavailable. The record therefore cannot establish the total materiality of the possible error.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile 2025 OE to the cash-flow statement and normalization adjustments, verify removal of the $42.4m gain, isolate Houston's pre-sale revenue, costs and maintenance needs, and rerun the anchor excluding its sustainable OE while reconciling proceeds once.

audit_findings.title: VPP accounting can introduce noncash revenue into perpetual owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $7.2m recognized in 2025, 0.66% of anchor OE; treating the full amount as perpetual would add approximately $101.2m or $0.77 per share to base value
audit_findings.mechanism: Unadjusted deferred-revenue recognition raises anchor OE and is then grown or carried into the terminal period despite representing cash received in 2012 and 2013.
audit_findings.evidence: The proceeds we received from the sale of the percentage interest were recorded as deferred revenue on the balance sheet.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the OE worksheet already offsets the deferred-revenue release remains unresolved, but its maximum identified 2025 amount is small. Even the conservative sensitivity of capitalizing the entire pretax $7.2m using the model's base operating-value-to-anchor multiple changes the $118.48 base value by only about 0.7%, and the actual finite-life effect would be smaller.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the $7.2m deferred-revenue release was removed or offset by the change in deferred revenue; correct the worksheet if necessary, without treating the finite VPP balance as terminal OE.

audit_findings.title: The known-instrument share ceiling omits director stock units
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; 2025 nonemployee-director stock-unit expense was $2.9m, but the outstanding unit count was not supplied
audit_findings.mechanism: Omitted director units understate the fully diluted share denominator and therefore overstate value per share.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition to the share-based compensation plans for employees discussed above, we issue a limited number of stock units to our nonemployee directors annually.
